messages.content: What is the acceleration a ball will reach if it's thrown straight upwards with a velocity of 5 m/s?

function.name: calculate_maximum_height
function.description: Calculate the maximum height an object will reach if it's thrown straight upwards with an initial velocity, ignoring air resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

initial_velocity.description: The initial velocity in meters per second. This is a float type value.

gravity.description: The acceleration due to gravity in meters per second squared, default value is 9.8. This is a float type value.

message.content:
The acceleration of the ball is determined by the force acting on it—in this case, gravity.  
Gravity provides a constant downward acceleration of about **9.8 m/s²** (on Earth).  
That value does **not** depend on the ball’s initial speed; whether you throw it at 5 m/s, 20 m/s, or even drop it from rest, the acceleration remains the same (ignoring air resistance).  

So, when you throw the ball straight upward at 5 m/s, it will still accelerate downward at roughly **9.8 m/s²** until it reaches its peak and then starts falling back down.
